adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:51 — Session type comes from userSession.isOffline(), but the offline session is only created later in generateRefreshToken, so the first access token from an offline_access request is encoded as "on" (online), and that online session may then be removed via FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` derives `SessionType` from `userSession.isOffline()` (or TRANSIENT), but it does not show (a) when/where an offline session is created (e.g., in `generateRefreshToken`) nor (b) any `FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` logic that would remove an online session. The claim about offline session creation timing and subsequent removal cannot be verified from the provided diff alone, and it also assumes that an `offline_access` request should cause the *access token* to be marked offline, which is not established by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:108 — GRANT_TYPE is only set in createTokenResponse, ROPC, refresh, pre-auth and standard token exchange, so tokens from grants that call responseBuilder().generateAccessToken() directly (client_credentials, UMA permission, V1 token exchange) plus implicit/hybrid tokens all get the "na" grant shortcut.

adjudication.rationale: From the diff, grant type is captured in `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`) and then written into `ClientSessionContext` in the common helper `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)` (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType());`). The finding asserts that specific grants (client_credentials, UMA permission, v1 token exchange) bypass this and call `responseBuilder().generateAccessToken()` directly, but none of those flows’ implementations are shown in the diff, so that claim is not verifiable here and may be incorrect if they use `createTokenResponse`. The only verifiable fact is that tokens will get the "na" shortcut when `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` isn’t set; the diff does not prove that the listed grants/implicit-hybrid tokens necessarily fall into that bucket.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — getShortcut() is a new abstract method with no default, so an existing custom grant factory throws AbstractMethodError, and one returning null throws an NPE on ConcurrentHashMap.put in the encoder's postInit, which aborts server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (no default implementation). This is a binary-incompatible change for existing third-party factories compiled against the previous interface and can result in `AbstractMethodError` when `getShortcut()` is invoked (e.g., in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, which unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`). Additionally, `postInit` does `new ConcurrentHashMap<>().put(grantShortcut, grantName)` with no validation; if an implementation returns `null`, `ConcurrentHashMap` will throw NPE and abort startup. The diff itself doesn’t show any built-in factory returning null, so it’s primarily an extensibility/backward-compatibility concern rather than a guaranteed defect in the core code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:109 — encodeTokenId never checks that the grant shortcut is 2 characters with no ':', so a custom grant with a longer shortcut issues jti values that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with IllegalArgumentException.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, the encoded context is built as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort + ':' + rawId, but there is no validation that grantShort is exactly 2 characters and contains no ':'. However, getTokenContextFromTokenId strictly requires the pre-colon "encodedContext" to be length 6 and parses the last 2 chars as the grant shortcut. Therefore, any OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation returning a shortcut not exactly 2 chars (or containing ':') will produce jti values that this same decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException, a correctness issue exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The rawTokenId null check runs requireNonNull on grantType instead, so a null rawTokenId gets through silently and is encoded as "xxxxxx:null".

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — The lazy map refresh for hot-deployed grants skips the duplicate-shortcut check done in postInit, so a new grant with a clashing shortcut quietly remaps it and old tokens decode to the wrong grant.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and validates uniqueness by comparing the two map sizes (duplicate shortcuts/IDs would be detected). However, the later lazy refresh paths bypass that check: getShortcutByGrantType() does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)` after loading a factory by id, and getGrantTypeByShortcut() does the same after finding a factory by shortcut. If a hot-deployed grant reuses an existing shortcut, the `put` into grantsByShortcuts will overwrite the previous mapping silently, so decoding token IDs using that shortcut could resolve to a different grant than originally intended. The diff shows no duplicate detection or prevention in these refresh branches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — The public copy constructor Context(Context) was removed from the SPI, which breaks any caller or extension using it, and grantType is now only derived from formParams.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it existed before and is now deleted), which is a source/binary API incompatibility for any code constructing a new Context by copying an existing one. The new `grantType` field is initialized only once in the remaining constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, and there is no alternative setter/copy path shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — New abstract getShortcut() has no default, so existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations no longer compile and throw AbstractMethodError during DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (line 74), which breaks server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface with no default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, Keycloak now iterates `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories, casts to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any existing provider factory (including extensions) compiled against the previous interface version and loaded at runtime would throw `AbstractMethodError` when `getShortcut()` is invoked, potentially breaking server startup. This is a verifiable compatibility break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:103 — Removes the public Context(Context) copy constructor from a public SPI class with no deprecation step, which breaks extensions that subclass or wrap the grant Context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `OAuth2GrantType.Context` removes the previously available copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` (lines shown deleted in `OAuth2GrantType.java`), leaving only the main constructor and adding a new `grantType` field. Since `Context` is a `public static` nested class used in the grant SPI package, removing a public constructor is an API-breaking change for any external code that relied on copying/wrapping contexts via `new Context(existingContext)`. This is a compatibility concern rather than a runtime defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1054 — Every access token jti (and the TOKEN_ID event detail) changes from a bare UUID to "<6-char ctx>:<uuid>" with no opt-in, versioning or migration note, which breaks resource servers, event listeners and log correlation that treat jti as a UUID.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an intentional, unconditional change to access token IDs: in TokenManager.initToken the jti is no longer a bare UUID but is produced by TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx), which formats it as "<6-char ctx>:<raw uuid>" (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId). Tests were updated to expect this new format in event Details.TOKEN_ID (AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)), indicating planned behavior rather than an accidental defect. However, the finding’s compatibility concern is diff-grounded: there’s no opt-in/flag or versioned fallback in TokenManager; all new access tokens change jti format, which can impact external consumers that assume UUID.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — The lazy-refresh paths (lines 113 and 131) skip the shortcut-uniqueness check done in postInit, so a hot-deployed grant with a duplicate shortcut silently overwrites the mapping and later decodes to the wrong grant type.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() a uniqueness check is performed indirectly by comparing grantsByShortcuts.size() vs grantsToShortcuts.size(), which would catch duplicate shortcuts at boot time. However, the lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() (the on-demand “new grant deployed” code) do unchecked puts into the same maps: grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) can overwrite an existing shortcut->grant mapping, and grantsToShortcuts.put(newGrantType, shortcut) can create multiple grantType->sameShortcut entries. No validation is re-run, so a dynamically added grant with a duplicate shortcut can silently change decoding behavior for that shortcut (decode returns the last stored grant). This is a correctness defect in the new lazy-refresh logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Null check for rawTokenId re-checks grantType instead, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and encodes as "xxxxxx:null".

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId uses the wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of 4,6) and an inverted condition (missing "!"), so the matcher never checks the grant shortcut and the updated event assertions pass for any grant.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the token context prefix is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grant shortcut) per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, so the grant shortcut should be checked with substring(4, 6). The matcher instead uses substring(3, 5), and the condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected shortcut rather than requiring it. As a result, for most inputs it only validates the UUID part and does not enforce the expected grant shortcut, making the updated event assertions too permissive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.java:39 — client_credentials (and UMA permission) grants build tokens without going through createTokenResponse and never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE, so their token IDs silently get the "na" grant instead of "cc"/"pg".

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OAuth2GrantType.Context now captures `grantType` from `formParams` and `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)` unconditionally sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())`. Whether the client_credentials and UMA permission grant implementations "never go through createTokenResponse" (and therefore fail to set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`) is not shown in this diff, and no code for those grant `process(...)` methods is included here. From the diff alone, the alleged missing GRANT_TYPE for those flows cannot be verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:75 — Grant shortcuts are never checked to be non-null, exactly 2 chars, and free of ':' (the SPI javadoc even suggests 3 letters), so a custom grant can NPE at startup or produce token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with "Expected length of 6".

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), each OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contributes a shortcut via gtf.getShortcut() which is inserted into ConcurrentHashMaps without validation. ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys, so a custom grant returning null would NPE during postInit. Additionally, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() hard-requires the encoded context length to be exactly 6 and assumes the grant shortcut is exactly 2 chars (sessionType 2 + tokenType 2 + grantType 2). If a custom grant uses a shortcut of different length (the new javadoc even suggests “3-letters shortcut”) or containing ':', encodeTokenId() can generate token IDs that decoding rejects ("Expected length of 6") or misparses due to the ':' delimiter. This mismatch/absence of validation is introduced by the diff and can break behavior when custom grants are installed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 — testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, so it passes on the NPE from the null sessionFactory (postInit never called) rather than on the intended IllegalArgumentException.
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both point out that the test is catching a generic RuntimeException, which is overly broad and can mask unintended exceptions (e.g., NPE). The intended behavior is to assert the specific IllegalArgumentException thrown by the implementation, so the catch/expectation should be narrowed to that type for precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — The public Context copy constructor was removed, which breaks existing callers/extensions, and grantType is only taken from formParams at construction, so setFormParams leaves it stale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it existed before and is now gone), which is a source/binary incompatible change for any existing code that invoked it. Also, `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but `setFormParams(...)` only replaces `formParams` and does not recompute `grantType`, so subsequent updates to form parameters can leave `context.getGrantType()` stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109 — Grant-type note is set ad hoc at 5+ scattered call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase, ROPC:134, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType:82, StandardTokenExchangeProvider:237, TokenManager:248) instead of one central place, so any grant path that forgets it silently encodes "na".

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` being set in multiple disparate places (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` sets it from `context.getGrantType()`, while other flows set it manually: `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process`, `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process`, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient`, and `TokenManager.validateToken` for refresh). The encoder (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`) explicitly falls back to `UNKNOWN` ("na") when the attribute is missing, so forgetting to set it would silently degrade the encoded token-id context rather than hard-fail. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture concern (centralization/consistency), but the diff alone does not prove a concrete broken behavior is introduced (there is an explicit fallback), so it's not a verifiable bug from the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237 — Token exchange (and PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType:82, TokenManager:248) hardcode grant constants while other grants use context.getGrantType(), which is inconsistent and duplicates the factory IDs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows several places setting `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` via hardcoded grant IDs rather than flowing it from an `OAuth2GrantType.Context`: e.g. `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);` and `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType` sets it to `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_TYPE`, while other grants now set it from `context.getGrantType()` (e.g. `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`). This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency/duplication concern (maintainability/DRY), but it is not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone because the hardcoded values match the factories’ `getId()` constants/spec values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — New abstract getShortcut() on a provider SPI has no default, so every existing custom grant-type factory breaks at compile time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. While Keycloak’s built-in grant factories in this PR are updated to implement it, any existing external/custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations would fail to compile against this change unless updated, making it a backward-incompatible SPI change (not a runtime defect within this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 — Javadoc says the shortcut is about 3 letters, but the encoder hardcodes exactly 2 chars (length 6, substring 4-6) and postInit never validates length, so the contract is undocumented and unenforced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` with Javadoc suggesting a “usually like 3-letters shortcut”, but the new token-id encoding/decoding logic assumes fixed-width 2-char fields: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires `encodedContext.length() == 6` and parses the grant shortcut as `substring(4, 6)`, and `encodeTokenId` concatenates `sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShort(?)` expecting the result to match that 6-char context. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` checks uniqueness but does not validate shortcut length. This is a real, diff-grounded contract/documentation/enforcement gap for the new SPI, though it won’t fail with the shortcuts added in this diff (all are 2 chars).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/Constants.java:207 — Constants.GRANT_TYPE just aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, so the clientSessionContext attribute key reuses the form-param name and adds indirection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, so the statement about aliasing/reusing the form-param name is factually true. However, the finding does not identify a concrete defect or a clearly important, diff-demonstrable problem—it's largely a subjective design/style preference about indirection and key naming, with no evidence in the diff that reusing `grant_type` as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute key causes incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84 — A package-private instance helper was made public static so the encoder SPI can call into a protocol-mapper base class, which couples encode to mappers instead of extracting a shared utility.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession)` changed from package-private instance method to `public static` (services/src/main/java/.../AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java), and the new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` calls it to derive `AccessTokenContext.TokenType`. This is a real, diff-grounded architectural concern: the new encoder SPI now depends on a protocol-mapper base class for what is effectively shared token-creation logic, increasing coupling and API surface. It’s not a direct functional defect, but a design issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — grantType is captured once from formParams in the constructor, but setFormParams() does not refresh it, so it can go stale.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, and a getter `getGrantType()` is added. The existing `setFormParams(...)` method remains but (per the diff) does not update `grantType`, so if any code updates the context’s form parameters through `setFormParams`, `getGrantType()` can diverge from the current `formParams`. The diff doesn’t show any call sites of `setFormParams`, so staleness is a real API/edge-case concern created by the change, but not a verifiable currently-triggered defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — The public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed from the private SPI with no connection to the stated intent, which breaks extensions that use it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java` was removed entirely, leaving only the primary constructor (which now also sets `grantType`). That is an API/signature change in the server-spi-private module and can break external extensions/providers that previously relied on copying `Context` via that constructor, even if the main product code compiles and runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Copy-paste bug: the rawTokenId null check actually tests grantType again, so rawTokenId is never validated.
matched_golden_ids: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same copy-paste mistake in AccessTokenContext: a null-check intended for rawTokenId mistakenly checks grantType again, so rawTokenId can be null without being validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:41 — grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are mutable package-private fields exposed only so the unit test can bypass postInit.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared with no access modifier (`Map<String, String> grantsByShortcuts; Map<String, String> grantsToShortcuts;`), making them mutable package-private state. The added unit test (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`) directly assigns to these fields (`factory.grantsByShortcuts = new HashMap<>(); ... factory.grantsToShortcuts = ...`) to avoid running `postInit(...)`. This is a real encapsulation/architecture concern introduced by the diff (testability achieved by exposing internal mutable state), but it’s not a directly verifiable runtime defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:106 — Lazy-refresh lookups duplicate the postInit registration logic and skip its duplicate-shortcut validation.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, grant shortcuts are collected and then validated for uniqueness via the `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()` check. However, the later lazy-refresh paths (`getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut`) also add entries to `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` when a new grant appears, but do so without re-running any duplicate-shortcut (or duplicate-id) validation and can silently overwrite existing mappings if a shortcut collides. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/maintainability concern tied to the newly added lazy-refresh behavior, but not a conclusively triggered defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:33 — The unknown-grant sentinel "na" differs from the enums' UNKNOWN shortcut "un", and the 6-char layout and offsets are magic numbers instead of values derived from the shortcut definitions.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider, the grant-type unknown sentinel is intentionally defined as a separate constant (UNKNOWN = "na") and is not tied to AccessTokenContext.SessionType/TokenType UNKNOWN shortcuts (both "un"), so the “differs from enums” part is not a verifiable defect. However, the token-id parsing/formatting hardcodes the 6-character context length and substring offsets (length==6, substrings 0..2, 2..4, 4..6) rather than deriving them from the shortcut definitions, which is a concrete maintainability/robustness concern introduced by this diff (changes to shortcut lengths would require manual updates).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.java:40 — Shortcuts are defined inconsistently: some factories expose GRANT_SHORTCUT constants (ac/rt/ci/dg) while others inline literals (cc/pg/pc/ro/te).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show inconsistency: AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory/RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory/CibaGrantTypeFactory/DeviceGrantTypeFactory define GRANT_SHORTCUT constants, while ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory/PermissionGrantTypeFactory/PreAuthorizedCodeGrantTypeFactory/ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantTypeFactory/TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory return inline literals ("cc","pg","pc","ro","te"). However this is a style/consistency concern, not a verifiable defect or behavior break introduced by the diff (all still implement getShortcut() correctly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The test matcher re-implements the token-id layout with the wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of (4,6)) and an inverted equals check, so the grant assertion is vacuous.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the matcher parses the encoded context prefix (`items[0]`) but uses `substring(3, 5)` even though the token-id layout introduced in this diff is 6 chars with the 2-char grant shortcut at indices `[4,6)` (sessionType 0-2, tokenType 2-4, grantType 4-6). Additionally, the check is inverted: `if (....equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` causes a mismatch when the expected shortcut is present, so the matcher effectively only asserts the raw id is a UUID and that the grant shortcut is *not* the expected one. This makes the grant assertion vacuous/incorrect as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — New abstract getShortcut() has no default, so existing custom grant factories compiled against the old SPI throw AbstractMethodError in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit and crash server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` then iterates `factory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` and calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any existing third-party/custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation compiled against the previous SPI (without `getShortcut`) would not have that method at runtime and would throw `AbstractMethodError` when `postInit()` invokes it, potentially failing server startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Grant shortcut is not validated at startup: a null shortcut NPEs on ConcurrentHashMap.put (opaque startup crash), and a shortcut that isn't exactly 2 chars is accepted even though the decoder rejects it.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, the code unconditionally does `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut(); grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);` with `grantsByShortcuts` as a `ConcurrentHashMap` (initialized just above). `ConcurrentHashMap` does not permit null keys/values, so an extension/implementation returning `null` from `getShortcut()` will cause an immediate NPE during startup/provider postInit, with no validation or clear error message. Also, there is no validation that shortcuts are exactly 2 characters even though `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` requires the encoded context length to be exactly 6 (2+2+2) and extracts `gtShortcut` as `substring(4, 6)`, so a non-2-char shortcut would lead to token IDs that the decoder will reject.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — Decoder requires a 6-char context, but the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory Javadoc suggests 3-letter shortcuts and encodeTokenId never checks length, so tokens from such grants encode fine but always fail to decode with IllegalArgumentException.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(), the decoder enforces an encoded context length of exactly 6 and parses the grant shortcut as a 2-char substring (substring(4, 6)). However, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut() is documented as “usually like 3-letters shortcut”, and encodeTokenId() concatenates the shortcut without validating its length. Therefore, a grant implementation following the Javadoc and returning a 3-letter shortcut would produce token IDs that encode successfully but always fail decoding with IllegalArgumentException due to the strict 6-char assumption.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:111 — encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for any grant-type attribute with no registered factory, and it runs inside initToken, so token issuance fails hard (500) when it could fall back to "na" as it already does for null.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TokenManager.initToken()` now always encodes the access token ID via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` (around line 111 in the new file), it calls `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` and throws `IllegalStateException` if the shortcut is `null`. `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` only substitutes `UNKNOWN` ("na") when the `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` attribute is **null**, not when it is set to an unrecognized value. Therefore, if any code path sets `clientSessionCtx` attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to a value that has no registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (or `getShortcut()` mapping), token issuance will fail hard. This is a real robustness/edge-case concern introduced by the change, but the diff does not show a concrete standard-flow path that sets an unregistered grant type, so it’s not a clearly verifiable functional bug in the shown code alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — Lazy map refresh skips the duplicate-shortcut check from postInit and updates the two maps non-atomically, so a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and older tokens decode to the wrong grant.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() validates duplicate shortcuts only once by comparing map sizes after initially populating grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts. However, the later lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() mutate both ConcurrentHashMaps with plain put() calls and do not re-check for shortcut collisions. If a newly discovered/deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returns a shortcut already present, grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) will overwrite the existing shortcut->grant mapping (and the reverse mapping is updated separately), which can cause decoding of existing token IDs with that shortcut to resolve to the wrong grant rather than failing fast. The diff explicitly introduces this lazy refresh behavior and the non-validated overwriting risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Copy-paste bug null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId, so a null raw id silently encodes as "xxxxxx:null".

adjudication.rationale: In the new AccessTokenContext constructor, the null-check intended for rawTokenId is mistakenly written as `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` later appends `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield an encoded token id ending with `:null`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId uses the wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of 4,6) and inverted logic (returns false on match), so the grant-shortcut check never fails and every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/device/CIBA assertion silently passes for any grant type.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the matcher extracts the grant shortcut via `items[0].substring(3, 5)` and then returns `false` when it equals `expectedGrantShortcut`. Per the encoding logic added in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider (`sessionType[0..2) + tokenType[2..4) + grant[4..6)`), the grant shortcut should be `substring(4, 6)`, and equality should be required (return false on mismatch, not on match). As written, the grant-type check is effectively broken (typically never triggers due to wrong offset, and even if it did it rejects correct values), so event assertions won’t actually validate the expected grant shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 — testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, so it passes via an NPE from the null sessionFactory in getGrantTypeByShortcut rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()`, the factory’s `sessionFactory` is never set (no `postInit` call). In `testIncorrectGrantType`, `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")` leads to `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")`, which returns null from `grantsByShortcuts` and then dereferences `sessionFactory` in the refresh path, causing an NPE. Because the test catches any `RuntimeException`, it passes even though it likely intended to assert an `IllegalArgumentException` from the provider logic. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue, not necessarily a runtime defect in production where `postInit` should initialize `sessionFactory`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:41 — Test hand-populates grant maps and skips postInit, so real factory init with real OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcuts, duplicate-shortcut detection, and lazy map refresh are never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()` calls `factory.init(null)` but then directly assigns `factory.grantsByShortcuts` and `factory.grantsToShortcuts` and instantiates `new DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider(null, factory)` without running `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`. As a result, the behavior added/relied upon in `postInit`—loading real `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations via `getProviderFactoriesStream`, validating duplicate shortcuts (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())`), and the lazy refresh paths that depend on `sessionFactory` in `getShortcutByGrantType` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut`—is not exercised by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:45 — getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (transient/offline/online, lightweight detection, null grant type fallback to "na") has no test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(): it derives SessionType from UserSessionModel persistence/offline state, derives TokenType via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and falls back grantType to "na" when clientSessionContext lacks Constants.GRANT_TYPE. The added unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) exercises only getTokenContextFromTokenId() and encodeTokenId(), and never constructs a ClientSessionContext/UserSessionModel to cover getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(), so the finding that this new method lacks test coverage is accurate and specific to the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1054 — Every access token's jti format changed, but no integration test checks the encoded grant for password, client_credentials, token exchange, UMA, pre-authorized code, or the refresh path (TokenManager.java:248), and the only matcher that tries is broken.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token IDs to an encoded form (`TokenManager.initToken`: `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`). The updated integration-test matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` is logically incorrect: it returns `false` when the grant shortcut matches (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`) and it slices the wrong indices for the 2-char grant shortcut (grant occupies chars 5-6 in the 6-char prefix, i.e., `substring(4,6)`), so it will reject valid token IDs. This is a concrete, verifiable defect introduced in the diff. (The lack of coverage for other grants is an additional test-gap concern, but the matcher being broken is itself a real bug.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — No tests for malformed encoded ids: wrong prefix length, unknown session-type or token-type shortcut, or extra ':' in the raw id.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial parsing/validation logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId (checks for ':' presence, enforces encodedContext length==6, validates sessionType/tokenType/grantType shortcuts and throws IllegalArgumentException on unknown values). The added unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest covers success cases, unknown/incorrect grant type, and the legacy no-colon format, but does not cover other malformed-id branches mentioned: encodedContext wrong length (length != 6), unknown session-type shortcut, unknown token-type shortcut, or inputs with additional ':' (which are accepted by splitting only on the first ':' and are untested). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The rawTokenId null check actually validates grantType a second time, and no test covers a null rawTokenId, which let the copy-paste bug through.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null-check is a copy/paste error: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` should validate `rawTokenId` but instead re-validates `grantType`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected, potentially causing later failures (e.g., in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` when concatenating `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`). The added tests cover parsing/encoding but do not include a case with `rawTokenId == null`, which would have exposed this defect.
